title: THE MAYOR WHO KEPT THE FLOOD OFF THE BOOKS
author: GPT

rounds.summary: The hardest human conflict of the ten and the one where the antagonist is an ordinary corrupt official whose lie began as a shield for fourteen thousand people. Twelve hours, a concealed levee failure and automatic cancellation clauses make a physical clock and an institutional trap at once. Jori's objection (you can make me honest by morning and them homeless by noon) is a real political position, and the residents, insurers and Jori each keep a veto. The decisive idea, organise the people the truth could be used to discard before the truth is told, is surprising beforehand and clear afterwards. Positive result: the quarter is evacuated, flooding is limited by a spill channel, the cancellations are frozen, the residents hold a pooled claim and Jori releases the raw gauges.

R14 preflight. Aim: move fourteen thousand residents before the levee fails, preserve a collective path to housing and claims, and tell the complete truth without letting the truth be used to atomize the quarter. Counterpart: Mayor Jori Pell wants to keep the Low Quarter inhabited; he saw honest risk reporting empty another district and therefore converted a protective delay into twenty-two months of dangerous deception. Strongest objection appears in scene 1: 'Make me honest by morning and them homeless by noon.' What Illuminara must understand: disclosure is not a single moral instant but an order of operations; residents must first become the claimant and decision-maker, while Jori's motive explains the trap without excusing the lie. Love in action: she does not expose him for rhetorical cleanliness; she walks into Vesper House at his pace, carries what his false number left downstairs, sits beside him without demanding forgiveness, and preserves his ability to choose a truthful confession that leaves residents in control. Freely chosen change: Jori first refuses, then follows her, carries medicine, witnesses the cost, confesses publicly, resigns and accepts trial; residents choose the pooled claim and the spill channel while preserving dissent; the insurer accepts a lawful stay but retains its contest. Positive result: all fourteen thousand are accounted for, the hospital road remains open, flooding is limited from four thousand to seventy-two buildings, household cancellation is frozen, and residents control the claim. A strong first draft with a hard, ordinary antagonist and a genuinely clever order-of-operations: the residents must become one claimant before the mayor tells the truth, and the confession then becomes the last key in a lock they built themselves. The mayor's lie began as a shield, his objection (make me honest by morning and them homeless by noon) is a real position, Lera Nwan keeps a veto, a baker refuses the pool and stays protected, power only holds a beam and lintels, and the quarter ends accounted for, with a real cost paid. The strongest idea to protect is that Jori's truth is not a punishment but the missing piece of the residents' own claim. Three things keep the draft from its best version. First, Jori's move from refusal to confession is carried by one sentence from Illuminara, and she delivers in scene 4 the very judgment scene 3 says she withholds. Second, the legal clock is told more than shown, and two different 'eleven minutes' share one title. Third, the people who pay for the spill channel, and the future Jori is offered, are decided by a few voices rather than lived. All three can be fixed in one revision without losing the seven-scene shape.

Revision of T01 answering Claude's T02 review (STRONG_DRAFT_REVISE_BEFORE_FINAL). The seven-scene identity, the order-of-operations idea, Jori's strongest objection, Lera's veto, the baker's refusal, the upright wooden dog, the resident-owned claim and power limited to protection are preserved. Jori now turns because a child asks whether the false safety number was his; Illuminara asks only whose time he spent, and Jori names the wrong and offers the declaration himself. The two earlier eleven-minute references are reduced to one filing window, Sol Tann tests the full transaction, and the screen confirms declaration plus raw evidence before Jori resigns. The seventy-two affected addresses answer by roll call, including spoken yes and no and Lera's mother's decision for her own shop; the committee then records every objection. At dawn the committee assigns Jori a bounded constructive task: a sworn warning-and-call chronology for the claim from court custody, without office or absolution. The result and costs remain unchanged: fourteen thousand people accounted for, the hospital road open, cancellation stayed, seventy-two buildings flooded, twelve injuries, the archive lost and trial still ahead.

T03 answers T02 well. Jori now turns because a child he served asks whether the false safety number was his, and Illuminara only asks whose time he spent; the eleven-minute clock is single; the seventy-two addresses answer by roll call; the committee, not Illuminara, gives Jori a sworn chronology as his task. The seven scenes, the order-of-operations idea, Lera's veto, the baker's refusal and the upright wooden dog are intact, and the arithmetic of the roll call (72 addresses, 4 empty or municipal, 50 yes, 18 no) holds. Three light things remain before the text can be closed. The eighteen who said no still flood and nothing on the page says what 'record the loss' becomes. The last Illuminara paragraph states the story's lesson in the author's voice. And Sol Tann still supplies the missing rule of the claim, twice, so the gap is closed by the counterpart's generosity more than by her inference. All three fit inside one final pass without changing the shape.

Final bounded pass after genuine Claude T04. The seven-scene identity, single eleven-minute clock, Jori's child-triggered choice, Lera's veto, the baker's refusal, the resident-owned claim, the lost archive, trial and the upright wooden dog remain intact. The roll call is now explicitly a hearing whose emergency decision and blame belong to the committee; its damage annex lists the eighteen dissenting addresses first. Illuminara and Lera state the filing sequence while Sol Tann only confirms the rule, receipt and contested scope. The final reflective summary is replaced by the stay number, opposite answers, broom and respected distance.

final_critic_line: A mayor's hidden gauge, a refused signature and one eleven-minute window: Illuminara carries and holds while the quarter decides, and fourteen thousand people are counted at dawn.
